items.fullText: 테크 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 "챗GPT부터 국산 AI까지 골라 쓴다"…KT 'AI 플랫폼' 승부수 입력 2026.10.27 16:06 수정 2026.10.27 16:10 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 라현진 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. 오픈라우터와 손잡고 AI 모델 500개 연결 국내 GPU로 7종 직접 구동 모델 자동 선택·보안·과금 통합 토큰 비용 최대 25% 절감 박윤영 대표 'AX 플랫폼 컴퍼니' 전략 구체화 박상원 KT AX사업부문장이 27일 서울 세종로 KT광화문빌딩에서 열린 기자간담회에서 '토큰팩토리' 사업에 대해 발표하고 있다. /사진=KT 제공 KT가 500개 이상의 인공지능(AI) 모델을 한곳에서 이용할 수 있는 플랫폼을 선보인다. 통신사업에서 쌓은 연결·과금·보안 역량을 앞세워 AI 플랫폼 시장을 선점하겠다는 목표다. 박윤영 KT 대표가 취임 후 내놓은 ‘AX 플랫폼 컴퍼니’ 전략이 구체화된 첫 번째 결과다. 업무별로 최적 AI 자동 선택 KT는 27일 서울 세종로 KT광화문빌딩에서 기자간담회를 열고 AI 플랫폼 ‘토큰팩토리’를 공개했다. 토큰팩토리는 하나의 응용프로그램인터페이스(API)로 국내외 AI 모델을 통합 제공하는 플랫폼이다. 이용자는 여러 AI 서비스를 개별적으로 구독할 필요 없이 하나의 플랫폼에서 모델 선택부터 사용량 확인, 비용 관리, 결제까지 처리할 수 있다. 오는 30일 기업 고객을 대상으로 정식 출시한다. 첫 출시 때는 73개 AI 모델을 제공하고 오는 12월에는 글로벌 AI 모델 중개 플랫폼 오픈라우터와 연계해 500개 이상으로 늘린다. 내년 3월에는 개인 개발자와 일반 이용자에게도 서비스를 제공할 계획이다. 핵심은 업무에 적합한 모델을 자동으로 골라 요청을 보내는 ‘모델 라우팅’이다. KT가 자체 개발한 ‘오토 모델 라우터’는 질문의 난이도와 요구 품질, 비용을 분석한다. 간단한 요약·번역에는 경량 모델을, 복잡한 추론에는 고성능 모델을 배정하는 방식이다. 입력 문장에서 불필요한 표현을 제거하는 압축 기술도 적용했다. KT에 따르면 프롬프트 압축으로 약 20%, 모델 자동 선택으로 약 5%의 비용 절감 효과를 낸다. 예컨대 ‘다음 주 출장인데 월요일 오전에 서울에서 부산으로 가는 KTX 열차를 찾아줘’라는 질문을 ‘다음 주 월요일 오전 서울 부산 KTX’로 압축하는 식이다. 질문의 의미를 유지하면서 AI가 처리해야 할 토큰 수를 줄여 비용과 응답 시간을 단축한다는 설명이다. 이진형 KT AX사업본부장이 27일 서울 세종로 KT광화문빌딩에서 열린 기자간담회에서 '토큰팩토리' 사업에 대해 발표하고 있다. /사진=KT 제공 토큰팩토리만의 차별점은 국내에서 AI 추론을 직접 수행한다는 것이다. AI 모델 7개는 국내 KT 데이터센터에서 구동된다. 업스테이지 ‘솔라 프로4’, KT ‘믿음 K3.0’, 모티프 ‘모티프3’ 등 국산 모델 3종과 지푸AI의 ‘GLM-5.3-플래시’, 구글 ‘젬마4-31B’ 등 해외 오픈웨이트 모델 4종이다. 오픈웨이트는 모델의 가중치가 공개돼 자체 인프라에서 구동할 수 있는 방식이다. 이진형 KT AX사업본부장은 “해외 모델 제공사와 별도 계약을 맺고 국내 데이터센터에서 직접 추론 서비스를 제공하기로 했다”며 “데이터 처리를 국내에서 수행하는 소버린 AI 환경을 구현하는 데 의미가 있다”고 말했다. 연내 오픈라우터를 입점시켜 글로벌 AI 모델 500개 이상을 확보할 예정이다. 이에 따라 국산 모델, 오픈웨이트

How OpenAI turned its coding tools into dots, an always-on personal assistant
items.d: Alexander Embiricos, the OpenAI executive responsible for dots, never wants to have a meeting with someone else's AI agent.
items.fullText: The always-on AI personal assistant, which keeps working in the background even when you aren’t asking it to, is this year’s answer to the question of how people will actually use deep learning models. The startup Instinct became an overnight sensation, and Meta put the full force of its marketing behind its assistant, Muse. OpenAI wasn’t going to be left out. The company released dots , its assistant offering, at its developer day in late September. Alexander Embiricos, who leads OpenAI’s enterprise product team, joined us at TechCrunch Disrupt this month to explain where the product came from—starting with the question of why so many companies seem to be turning to cutesy mascots as avatars for their trillion-parameter matrix multiplication machines. “There’s kind of this convergent evolution happening,” Embiricos said of the efforts to build AI assistants. “As we were working on the product, we realized if we could frame this as, it’s an entity and it’s a single conversation, not many different conversations….it starts to become intuitive.” The assistant is available in the ChatGPT desktop and mobile apps to subscribers on the Pro tier or higher, with plans starting at $100 a month. Once it is connected to your calendar, email, computer and other tools, the agent tries to help you get your work done. Embiricos points out that you could achieve much of dots’ functionality with Open AI’s Codex app, its coding tool, released at the beginning of this year. But that requires more work and hand-holding. He recalled celebrating when his wife started leaving her computer on all night so that her agents could keep working. “On the product team, what I think about is, how do we make this intuitive and useful to people?” he told Disrupt attendees. “A lot of that isn’t building some new piece of tech into the product; it’s how you frame it to the user and how it feels.

Anthropic’s IPO filing reveals its strategy for keeping enterprise customers hooked
items.d: Anthropic’s S-1 shows more than half of its $100,000-plus customers now use both the Claude Platform and a first-party app, a cross-selling playbook reminiscent of Amazon that’s making enterprise customers stickier.
items.fullText: Anthropic is building the same kind of cross-product ecosystem that helped make tech companies like Amazon and Uber enormously sticky, and its S-1 suggests the strategy is working. More than half of customers spending at least $100,000 annually now use both the Claude platform and a first-party app like Claude Code or Cowork, up from about 30% at the end of last year. “The speed and depth of our enterprise customer adoption are powerful evidence of Claude’s position at the frontier of AI,” the S-1, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday , reads. As of September 30, Anthropic recorded more than 11,900 customers spending at least $100,000; more than 1,900 customers spending upward of $1 million; and about 250 customers spending $10 million or more annually. Anthropic attributes customer momentum to a “significant usage expansion as customers realize the value of deploying Claude across their organizations,” which drove net revenue retention of about 900% as of the end of the third quarter. Throwing shade at the entire legacy SaaS industry, Anthropic pitches Claude as not a “static product that serves a single use case,” but rather “frontier AI with rapidly advancing capabilities” spanning the models, the developer platform, and the applications users interact with directly. “An advance at any layer compounds across all three layers, accelerating the pace at which we can deliver more capable intelligence,” the filing reads, calling this “integrated approach” the reason more customers use both the Claude Platform and first-party apps. The playbook is familiar. Uber began by selling rides but has expanded into food delivery and freight. With AWS, Amazon drew in customers with cloud computing services before expanding those relationships into storage, databases, and other offerings, making the ecosystem increasingly hard to leave. items.t: Anthropic officially files for its public debut
items.d: Anthropic has officially filed for an IPO, revealing soaring revenue, mounting losses, major enterprise adoption, and an unusual governance structure designed to preserve founder control and its AI safety mission.
items.fullText: After weeks of leaked S-1s , Anthropic finally filed for an initial public offering on Monday, setting the stage for one of the most closely watched public debuts in modern U.S. history. Anthropic, which plans to list under the ticker “ANT,” recorded revenue of $16.3 billion for the first half of 2026, up from $1.2 billion in the same period last year, according to the firm’s latest SEC filing. That revenue came off the back of an operating loss of $693 million, an improvement from the $2.1 billion in operating losses that Anthropic recorded in the first half of 2025. Anthropic’s net loss, however, hit $80.7 billion, which was largely driven by noncash accounting adjustments tied to convertible debt. The company says it “may not achieve or sustain profitability in the future.” The filing also provided more color on the scale of Anthropic’s enterprise business. As of the end of September, Anthropic had more than 11,900 customers spending $100,000 or more annually; 1,900 customers spending $1 million or more; and about 250 customers spending $10 million or more. As previously reported , Anthropic’s governance structure will enable Anthropic’s seven co-founders to maintain control once the company goes public. Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei, Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish, and Christopher Olah will make up the “Founder LLC,” which will collectively control 50.1% of shareholder voting power — a move Anthropic says is designed to preserve the company’s AI safety mission, per the filing. Anthropic’s Long-Term Benefit Trust, established in 2023 to ensure the company pursues its public benefit mission , will have the authority to appoint most of the company’s board. items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Anthropic reveals $80 billion loss, huge spending spree ahead of IPO The company warned that AI could “pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity” as cybersecurity fears grow. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 AI startup Anthropic unveils its public IPO filing for the first time 03:17 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 26, 2026, 9:12 AM EDT / Updated Oct. 26, 2026, 11:16 AM EDT By Steve Kopack Artificial intelligence startup Anthropic on Monday unveiled its public IPO filing ahead of what is expected to be one of the largest stock debuts in history. That offering, widely expected to come sometime in mid-November, could value the Claude developer at more than $2 trillion. That could surpass the current record holder, Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which raised $75 billion in an IPO in June that valued the rocket-AI-social-media firm at $2.1 trillion. The filing did not include a potential share price, the number of shares to be offered or a valuation for the whole company, all of which will be determined after Anthropic holds a “road show” with investors, prospective investors and its bankers. Monday’s filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission showed that Anthropic, like other AI firms, is splashing out unprecedented amounts of cash on cloud services to run its AI models. The company plans to spend at least $110 billion with Amazon for cloud services through April 2036 and another $120 billion with SpaceX through 2029. Anthropic also said it planned to spend $115 billion with Google and $45 billion with Microsoft, both through 2033, for computing infrastructure. The filing said that the company recorded revenue growth of “1,368% year over year for the three months ended June 30, 2026.” The cost of renting servers and chips grew by 300% over the same period. items.fullText: 테크 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 AI 에이전트 산업 확산, 보안·표준화가 관건…국회서 머리 맞댄다 입력 2026.10.26 15:05 수정 2026.10.26 15:05 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 안정훈 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. SKT·페르소나AI, 내달 5일 미래기술 전략포럼서 발제 인공지능산업협회(KAIIA)는 다음달 5일 오후 3시 국회 의원회관 제8간담회의실에서 '제3차 미래기술 전략포럼'을 개최한다고 26일 밝혔다. 이번 포럼은 AI 에이전트의 기술 발전과 산업 적용 가능성을 살펴보고, 신뢰성 확보와 정책적 대응 방안을 논의하기 위해 마련됐다. AI 에이전트는 단순한 정보 검색이나 질의응답을 넘어 사용자의 목표에 따라 작업을 계획하고 실행하는 기술이다. 기업 내부 데이터와 업무 시스템, 외부 응용프로그램 인터페이스(API) 등을 활용해 복잡한 업무를 자율적으로 수행할 수 있다는 점에서 차세대 AI 기술로 주목받고 있다. 이번 행사에서는 김지훈 SK텔레콤 AI사업본부장과 유승재 페르소나AI 대표가 발제자로 나선다. 두 발표자는 AI 에이전트 기술의 발전 방향과 실제 산업 현장에서의 활용 가능성을 소개할 예정이다. AI 에이전트 확산에 따른 기술적·제도적 과제도 주요 논의 대상이다. 자율적인 업무 수행 과정에서 발생할 수 있는 보안 위험과 데이터 보호 문제, 접근 권한 통제, 실행 이력 추적 및 감사, 시스템 간 상호운용성 확보 등이 핵심 의제로 다뤄진다. 발표 이후에는 산업계와 학계, 연구계 전문가들이 참여하는 질의응답과 라운드토크가 진행된다. AI 에이전트의 신뢰성을 높이기 위한 기술 검증과 표준화, 관련 제도 개선 방안 등을 논의할 예정이다. 미래기술 전략포럼은 AI와 반도체 등 국가 핵심 기술 분야의 산업 경쟁력 강화를 위해 출범한 민간 주도 협력체다. 지난 8월 31일 국회에서 첫 포럼을 개최한 이후 기술 개발과 정책, 표준화 등을 연계하기 위한 논의를 이어가고 있다. 안정훈 기자 ajh6321@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 안정훈 ADVERTISEMENT 관련 뉴스 1 주차하면 충전까지…쏘카, 전기차 결합상품 선보여 쏘카가 전기차 주차와 충전을 연계한 시범 서비스에 나섰다. 쏘카는 전기차 충전 플랫폼 ‘EV 인프라’를 운영하는 소프트베리와 전기차 주차·충전 연계 서비스 시범 운영을 위한... 2026.10.26 14:48 2 "공연장 이름까지 사버렸다"…네카오가 노리는 '1조 시장' 네이버와 카카오가 대형 공연장으로 사업 영토를 넓히고 있다. 수만 명이 모이는 공연장을 멤버십·결제·콘텐츠 등 기존 플랫폼 서비스를 확장하는 오프라인 거점으로 삼으려는 것이다. 빠르게 성장하... 2026.10.26 13:39 3 포스코DX, 美 페르소나AI에 200만 달러 베팅…"로봇 투자 확대" 포스코그룹이 미국 산업용 휴머노이드 로봇 전문기업에 투자해 자사의 인공지능(AI) 기술과 로봇이 접목된 피지컬AI를 현장에 확산시키기 위해 본격 나선다.포스코DX는 미국 산업용 휴머노이드 로봇 기업 페르소나AI에 2... 2025.12.23 10:03 ADVERTISEMENT 많이 본 뉴스 1 '이미 팔았는데'…삼성전자 100주 배당금 100만원이라고? 2026.10.25 11:43 2 치킨 값보다 싸네?…1만원짜리 가전 내놓자 다이소 '긴장' 2026.10.25 07:30 3 고수들의 투자비법 남들 던질 때 449억 담았다…10억 자산가들이 급락장에 찍은 두 종목 2026.10.25 10:46 4 "月 4억씩 팔아도 남는 게 없다"…정준하도 두 손 든 '줄폐업 공포' 2026.10.24 10:37 5 "이게 그 아빠차라고?"…G80보다 커진 '이 車' 타보니 2026.

items.fullText: NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations October 21, 2026 by Mavi Nafria 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! European retailers are using open models and physical intelligence across use cases — from a commerce platform cutting inference costs by 90% to to a fulfillment center where collaboration of different robotic fleets is simulated inside a digital twin. Frontier Results With Open Models Retail leaders and technology companies across Europe are using NVIDIA-accelerated open and frontier models to advance agentic commerce, digital product discovery and retail R&D. Shopify post-trains open models to reach frontier-level accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Its engineers use the NVIDIA Megatron Bridge library for faster fine-tuning and NVIDIA NeMo RL for reinforcement learning. Shopify has post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for the GraphQL subagent integrated into Sidekick, Shopify’s AI assistant for merchants. The subagent retrieves store data for several Sidekick features, including Sidekick Pulse, which researches a merchant’s store and recommends ways to improve it. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements On Shopify’s internal benchmark, the post-trained model surpasses a leading frontier model in accuracy while cutting serving costs by 90% and delivering responses 7x faster. Beyond Sidekick, NVIDIA CCluster vLLM inference optimization software helped Shopify achieve 4.5x faster performance and up to 12x lower inference cost across five additional use cases: catalog enrichment, merchant assistant, e-commerce shopping simulation, product taxonomy classification, and merchant and buyer recommendations. Zooplus , Europe’s leading online pet retailer, with Infosys and NVIDIA technologies rebuilt its product discovery stack for the agentic era. October 21, 2026 by Stuart Pitts 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design. NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Sovereign: AI Clouds Building European AI Infrastructure Europe is home to world-class research, engineering talent, industrial expertise, data, the next generation of models and applications that requires large-scale computing close to where that knowledge resides. Regional AI clouds provide the infrastructure foundation on which model builders, enterprises and entire industries can grow. As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence. Nscale is using the NVIDIA DSX Platform to coordinate power allocation with workload requirements. items.fullText: GTC Berlin 2026: Live Updates From NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang’s Keynote October 21, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Founded in a tent near the Berlin Wall in 1980, the Tempodrom moved several times before settling near Anhalter Bahnhof in 2001. Its permanent home has since hosted concerts, galas and political events. Today, it hosts a different kind of spectacle. GTC Berlin runs three days, with more than 100 sessions on agentic AI, robotics, physical AI, open models and accelerated computing underway at STATION-Berlin down the road. Here, journalists, analysts and partners have gathered for the main event: NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s keynote. Huang Takes the Stage Huang opened with a question: What do L’Oréal, Revolut, Spotify, Merck, Vodafone, Zara, Porsche, Nestlé and HSBC have in common? They’re all European companies and they’re all working with NVIDIA on AI, he said. The keynote comes on the heels of NVIDIA’s weeklong road across Europe — Paris, London, Stockholm, Dublin — with the company committing nearly $10 billion to the technology ecosystem across Europe and working with 12,000+ partners. “After decades of advancement in the computer industry, we are now at the beginnings of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements AI is a five-layer cake , Huang explained. Energy powers advanced computers that are part of an AI factory, which generates tokens and digital intelligence from the models that run on it, which are then integrated into every application. “Long before the AI models emerge, the infrastructure has to exist,” he said, highlighting how, similarly, the internet first needed networking, and electricity first required the grid. “To be part of this AI economy, you don’t want to just be consuming the AI; you want to be producing the AI,” Huang said. “We could do all of that here in Europe, and in fact, we’ve already started.” The AI Fac
